offence_severity: Minimum/Maximum: 302 IPC (death sentence), 363 IPC (imprisonment for life or rigorous imprisonment up to 7 years), 366 IPC (imprisonment up to 10 years), 377 IPC (imprisonment up to 10 years), 376(2)(f) IPC (imprisonment for life or rigorous imprisonment up to 10 years)
number_of_offences: Charged with multiple offences, but the judgment does not specify the exact number of counts upheld
key_evidence_accepted: The DNA report and FSL report formed the foundation of discussion by the High Court.
witness_credibility: The court noted that the examination of 13 witnesses within seven days and the lack of waiting for FSL and DNA reports raised concerns about the thoroughness of the process, but did not explicitly assess the credibility of the main witnesses.
trial_duration: The trial was concluded within a fortnight after the charges were framed on 19.02.2013. The trial court's judgment was dated 27.06.2013, and the High Court's judgment was dated 30.04.2009.
legal_representation: Counsel for the accused: Shri D.S. Chauhan. Counsel for the State: Shri B.L. Mandloi P.P.
investigation_status: Charge-sheet filed on 13.02.2013, trial completed by 27.06.2013, and the case was appealed to the High Court.
procedural_irregularity: The court noted that the Amicus Curiae was appointed on 19.02.2013, but was not given sufficient time to prepare for the defense, and the trial was concluded within a fortnight, which left glaring gaps in the process.

appeal_history.high_court: Conviction and death sentence confirmed, but the case was restored to the Supreme Court for reconsideration.
appeal_history.supreme_court: Judgment of conviction and orders of sentence set aside, and the matter was directed for de novo consideration.

prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the trial was expedited to ensure fair trial and that the process of framing charges and conducting the trial within a fortnight was necessary for the administration of criminal justice.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the accused was not given sufficient time to prepare for the trial, as the Amicus Curiae was appointed on the same day as the charges were framed, leaving no time for proper preparation and leading to a miscarriage of justice.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the right to free legal aid is an essential ingredient of a fair trial and that the process of expediting criminal trials must not compromise the fundamental elements of fairness and the opportunity for the accused to prepare their defense.
precedent_relied_upon: Bashira v. State of U.P., [1969] 1 SCR 32 : AIR 1968 SC 1313; Ambadas Laxman Shinde and Others v. State of Maharashtra (2018) 14 SCALE 730 : (2018) 18 SCC 788; Imtiyaz Ramzan Khan v. State of Maharashtra (2018) 9 SCC 160; Best Bakery case; Hussainara Khatoon and Others (IV) v. Home Secretary, State of Bihar, Patna (1980) 1 SCC 98 : [2012] 6 SCR 1182
other_sentence_order: The Court directed de novo consideration of the case, allowing the counsel to make submissions on whether the charges should be amended, whether any prosecution witnesses need to be recalled for cross-examination, and whether expert evidence is required in response to the FSL and DNA reports. The Court also laid down norms for the appointment of Amicus Curiae in cases involving life or death sentences.
